---
title: "Labs"
toc: false
---

Browser labs for the course's hardest ideas. Everything runs in your browser;
no installs, no server. Each lab follows one loop: **predict** before moving a
control, **manipulate** one quantity at a time, **observe** the exact
consequence, **explain** it in ordinary language, and **transfer** an object to
Stata for the problem set.

Every output says whether it is a live calculation, a stored simulation result,
or a conceptual illustration. Illustrative bands are never presented as
estimated uncertainty.

| Lab | Misconception it exposes | Lecture |
|-----|--------------------------|---------|
| [Shock-to-Response Explorer](01-shock-to-response-explorer.qmd) | That a response is estimated from one episode | 1 |
| [Transformation Workbench](02-transformation-workbench.qmd) | That an accumulated change is an accumulated level | 2 |
| [Identification and Controls Sandbox](03-identification-sandbox.qmd) | That "I included controls" is an identification argument | 3 |
| [Instrument and Multiplier Laboratory](04-instrument-multiplier-lab.qmd) | That a strong first stage establishes causality | 4 |
| [Confidence-Interval Coverage Simulator](05-coverage-simulator.qmd) | That a narrower interval is a more reliable one | 5 |
| [Claims About a Curve](06-claims-about-a-curve.qmd) | That "significant here, insignificant there" tests a difference | 6 |
| [Bias–Variance Laboratory](07-bias-variance-lab.qmd) | That a smoother curve is a better estimate | 7 |
| [Smoothing Workbench](08-smoothing-workbench.qmd) | That the fitted shape came from the data | 8 |
| [State-Dependence Laboratory](09-state-dependence-lab.qmd) | That an interaction identifies a fixed-state experiment | 9 |
| [Causal-Weight Explorer](10-causal-weight-explorer.qmd) | That a moved coefficient means a moved response function | 10 |
| [Where Does Identification Come From?](11-panel-identification.qmd) | That more rows mean more identifying information | 11 |
| [Clean-Control Builder](12-clean-control-builder.qmd) | That already-treated units are valid controls | 12 |
| [Counterfactual and Sensitivity Workbench](13-counterfactual-workbench.qmd) | That a reproduced calculation is a policy experiment | 13 |
| [Replication Referee Desk](14-replication-referee-desk.qmd) | That a matching figure means a sound analysis | 14 |
